title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: DOUG'S STEPSON
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Doug Hensley, a bug man from Knoxville, Tennessee.
Doug can talk a raccoon out of an attic. Last spring, he married Angela.
But her twenty-year-old son, Jordan, would not say one word to him.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE TALKER
segments.quote: Seek first to understand, then to be understood.
segments.author: Stephen Covey
lines: Doug tried dad jokes, ballgame tickets, and a forty-minute talk about termites.
Jordan just said, I'm good.
Then Doug remembered a line from Stephen Covey, taped up in his van:
Seek first to understand, then to be understood.
So Doug just watched. Every night, Jordan stood by his grandpa's old Jeep. Dead for three years.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE KEYS
segments.quote: To be trusted is a greater compliment than to be loved.
segments.author: George MacDonald
lines: One rainy morning, Jordan's ride to work never showed.
Doug thought of a line from George MacDonald, the Scottish writer:
To be trusted is a greater compliment than to be loved.
He tossed Jordan the keys to his work truck. The one with a giant cockroach on the roof.
Jordan stared like it was a hundred-dollar bill.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE MAILBOX
segments.quote: A stiff apology is a second insult.
segments.author: G. K. Chesterton
lines: That night, Jordan backed into the mailbox. The cockroach survived. The mailbox did not.
Doug yelled. Then he gave a stiff little speech.
Angela read him a line from G. K. Chesterton, the English writer:
A stiff apology is a second insult.
So Doug knocked on Jordan's door. I yelled. I was wrong. That mailbox was leaning anyway.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE PASSENGER SEAT
segments.quote: The heart has its reasons of which reason knows nothing.
segments.author: Blaise Pascal
lines: A week later, Jordan's dad in Ohio canceled his visit. Again.
Jordan sat alone in the dead Jeep. Doug walked out with a speech ready.
Then he remembered Blaise Pascal, the French thinker:
The heart has its reasons of which reason knows nothing.
So Doug kept the speech in his pocket, climbed in, and just sat there.
Finally Jordan said, Grandpa and I were going to fix this. Doug said, I've got Saturdays.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE BACKFIRE
segments.quote: A good laugh is sunshine in a house.
segments.author: William Makepeace Thackeray
lines: Every Saturday, they worked on that Jeep. Doug knew bugs, not engines.
In March, the Jeep coughed, went bang, and blew black smoke all over them.
They looked like two raccoons. Jordan laughed so hard he cried.
Angela said her grandma's favorite line, from the English novelist Thackeray:
A good laugh is sunshine in a house.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE CARD
segments.quote: The bond that links your true family is not one of blood, but of respect and joy in each other's life.
segments.author: Richard Bach
lines: By June, the Jeep ran. On Father's Day, Doug got a card from Jordan, with a line from Richard Bach, the pilot and writer:
The bond that links your true family is not one of blood, but of respect and joy in each other's life.
Underneath, Jordan wrote: Thanks for the Saturdays. The mailbox is still your problem.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Listen first. Trust. Say sorry right. Sit with the hurt. Laugh together. Choose family.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Listen first. Trust people. Say sorry like you mean it. Sit with the hurt. Laugh together. Choose your family.
I fixed a car once. Well, I held the flashlight.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
